proposal.thesis: LPL Financial is an independent-advisor platform, not a SaaS FCF machine: cash-sweep and advisory fees are the engine (stack_cards demand_driver=financials). Q2 ended 2026-06-30 printed company-reported revenue $5.187B, +35% YoY vs $3.835B, net income $379M / $4.74 diluted EPS, adjusted EPS $5.84, gross profit $1.618B, and $2.6T client assets with $23.6B net new assets (Q2 2026 earnings release, 2026-07-30). I am using the company's +35% figure, not the digest's 41.3% on the same $5.187B print (same source-conflict shape as BKNG). YTD free cash flow through 2026-06-30 is +$327M; TTM FCF of -$931M is deteriorating because of Atria/Commonwealth acquisition cash, not because the operating model stopped converting — they bought back $309M in Q2, authorized another $2.5B, and leverage is 1.91x inside the 1.5-2.5x target. The 6-month chart already did the pullback: a ~$378 high, a wick to ~$343, then a hold of the 20-day (~$362) that today's $370.14 close (price_as_of 2026-08-31) bounced from. Stop sits under that wick at $342 (8.1% / ~2.3x ATR 2.64%, above the 2.67% noise floor and inside the 5.34% expected-move band so a normal week can live). Target $432 is a re-rate toward ~14.5x FY27 EPS $29.74, which is 16% above entry and 2.0:1 from the $342 stop, through the 52-week high (~$399, 7.2% up). Sized at ~$120 as a 50-70% starter on the 1% risk budget. Next print 2026-10-29 is 59 days out — this 50-day hold is around that binary, not through it.

proposal.risk_map: This fails if: (1) today's Sierra Ridge OSJ move — ~40 advisors and ~$2.1B AUA leaving LPL for Cetera after 13 months, an Atria-vintage team (Cetera PR / Wealth Management, 2026-08-31) — is the start of Atria-integration leakage rather than an 8bp rounding error on $2.6T; early tell is Q3 net new assets well below Q2's $23.6B. (2) TTM FCF stays deeply negative because Commonwealth/Atria cash needs do not roll off, which would cap the multiple even if EPS keeps beating. (3) One discretionary officer/director sale sits inside a $1.91M 120-day sell notional (notable_discretionary_selling; six of seven prints are 10b5-1) — not a cluster, but it belongs on the risk stack. (4) A daily close back through $342, which is under last week's ~$343 wick and the 20-day, proves the bounce was a failed flag. Options: expected move 5.34% into 2026-09-18, ATM IV 33.4%, P/C volume 0.15 (slight_bullish, LOW confidence). Softening MTUM is why this is a financials seat, not a reason to stand down.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: 14 analysts rate it a buy (mean 1.75) with a $431.86 mean target, +16.7% vs the $370.14 close; forward P/E 12.4 vs a financials-broker sector median 18.67 (pe_n=18) and 30-day EPS revisions +2.41%. MY VIEW: the tape is treating today's $2.1B Sierra Ridge defection and a -$931M TTM FCF print as evidence the Atria/Commonwealth build is leaking advisors and cash, which is why a 35% growth book still sits at 12.4x. MECHANISM: $2.1B is 8 basis points of $2.6T and about 9% of one quarter's $23.6B net new assets; YTD FCF through 2026-06-30 is already +$327M and they spent $309M on buybacks in Q2, so the TTM hole is acquisition timing, not a broken cash engine — cash-sweep revenue also does the opposite of what a rate-cut NII model assumes while the 10-year is 4.67% and rising. RESOLUTION: the Q3 FY2026 print, currently dated 2026-10-29, showing net new assets still above $15B and Core G&A inside the lowered $2.14-2.165B 2026 guide.
